title: A Wolf for the Thorn
premise: Exiled storm-caller Coral Zhou discovers her name and today's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy, foretelling the death of King Aldric of Thornfell at the hands of 'the wolf beneath the crown.' When assassins strike and Coral saves the king instead, she becomes both suspect and savior, forced to navigate smuggler roads and court intrigue to unbind the ancient entity possessing the throne. Her ally, the king's bastard brother Wren, turns out to be the wolf's intended vessel, and Coral must choose between the prophecy's promise of justice and the loyalty she's come to feel. In the end, Coral shatters the binding at the cost of her storm-gift, leaving Wren mortal and free, the throne held by a regent council, and Coral exiled no longer but forever changed.
about_author: Marguerite Thackeray is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy steeped in the politics of borderlands, where loyalty is a currency and every road has a price.

chapters.title: The Date in the Margins
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Smuggling a cargo of banned storm-glass through Thornfell's high passes, Coral shelters in a ruined library and finds a prophecy naming her, the king, and tonight's date. She dismisses it as a smuggler's trick until the words rearrange before her eyes. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as the impossible becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Wolf Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. In the capital, the king wakes with blood on his hands and no memory of the night, while the crown whispers to him of debts owed. His court hides its fear behind ceremony. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread, a man trapped inside his own body, suspecting the truth he cannot speak.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Sorrow Bridge
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following the prophecy's geography, Coral is ambushed on the Sorrow Bridge by crown assassins who call her 'the storm-bringer.' She kills them with her gift and flees, realizing someone in the palace wants her dead before the prophecy's date. Emotional beat: fury and survival instinct hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bastard of Thornfell
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Wren POV. Wren, the king's illegitimate half-brother, intercepts Coral in a border town and offers alliance: he believes the crown is devouring Aldric and needs a storm-caller to break it. Neither trusts the other. Emotional beat: wary, prickly partnership born of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: What the Smugglers Remember
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral trades favors with old smuggling contacts to learn the prophecy's origin: a storm-caller named Yara was executed a century ago by the first Aldric, and her binding curse passed into the royal line. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by guilt, as Coral realizes her exile and Yara's share a root.

chapters.title: The Court of Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Coral infiltrate the capital during a mourning festival. Wren confronts Aldric privately and finds his brother still fighting inside, leaving coded messages in the king's letters. But the crown's entity notices Wren and marks him as its next vessel. Emotional beat: hope kindled, then terror as the enemy turns its gaze.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral discovers the court spymaster has been feeding the entity's agents information for years, and that Wren's name appears in the prophecy as 'the wolf.' She must decide whether Wren is victim or weapon. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting and the painful weight of loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: Storm over the Coronation Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The entity, sensing the prophecy closing, forces Aldric to summon the court to a midnight rite on the Coronation Road. Coral calls a storm to delay it, burning through her reserves, while Wren rides into the trap knowingly. Emotional beat: desperate, exhilarating sacrifice, the storm as both weapon and elegy.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. In the rite's heart, Coral finds Yara's original binding and the choice it offers: kill the vessel and end the entity forever. Instead, she pours her storm-gift into unbinding, severing the entity from both Aldric and Wren at the cost of her own power. Emotional beat: transcendent grief, love choosing mercy over justice.

chapters.title: After the Rain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, resolution. Weeks later: Aldric, freed but broken, abdicates to a regent council; Wren, no longer the wolf, offers Coral a home she no longer needs to smuggle her way into. Coral, giftless but unexiled, plants Yara's restored name in the rebuilt library. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace, and a new beginning without the storm.
